summary: Gwalior Airport (GWL) serves the historic city of Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh, India, sharing its grounds with the Gwalior Air Force Station in a dual-use civilian-military arrangement. The airport provides vital connectivity to one of North India's most heritage-rich destinations, home to the iconic Gwalior Fort and the former Scindia royal family. It primarily operates domestic flights linking Gwalior to major hubs like Delhi and Mumbai.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Gwalior Airport?
A: Gwalior Airport is mainly served by Air India, IndiGo, and SpiceJet, offering domestic flights to Delhi, Mumbai, and select other cities.

Q: How far is the airport from Gwalior city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 8-10 km from the city center and Gwalior Fort, typically a 20-25 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does Gwalior Airport have international flights?
A: Currently, Gwalior Airport primarily handles domestic flights, though infrastructure upgrades have been planned to support future international operations.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: The airport operates during scheduled flight hours; it is not a 24-hour facility, so check with your airline for terminal opening times.
transport_tips: Prepaid taxi counters and app-based cab services like Ola and Uber are available at the airport for the short ride into Gwalior city. Auto-rickshaws can be hired outside the terminal for budget-friendly transfers, though negotiating the fare in advance is recommended. Private car rentals can also be arranged through hotels in advance for added convenience.
local_tip: If you have a layover or a few hours to spare, request a quick stop at the nearby Gwalior Fort—one of India's largest and most impressive hill forts, just a short drive from the airport and visible from the runway on approach.
